evidence: The libev default loop (EV) is shared with the Twiggy server the test forks: segmentation fault in ev_feed_event on the fork child.

The libev default loop (AnyEvent on EV) is shared with the server Test::TCP forks; a watcher DESTROY in one edits the loop's arrays the other uses: segmentation fault in ev_check_stop on the fork child.

The libev loop (AnyEvent on EV) is shared with the task server each of these tests forks: segmentation faults in the parent's event loop while the server child runs. The time-out tests' faults, which also happen without a fork, are not attributed.
The libev loop (AnyEvent on EV) is shared with the test server it forks: segmentation faults on the fork child.

The libev loop (Mojo::Reactor::EV) is shared with the news server the tests fork: the server child traps in the loop and ends, so the client's pages come back empty, and the parent also faults in its loop.
The builder's C state is shared with the writer child the test forks: segmentation fault in the parent after the child ended.
The DBD::SQLite handle of Minion's SQLite backend is shared with the job processes Minion forks: invalid free and segmentation fault in the parent after the children ended.
The C memory of its XS modules is shared with the worker processes it forks: double frees on the fork children.

Parent and child both use one cache object, whose C struct (lock state, locked page) they share instead of each having its own: the parent croaks that a page is already locked (the child's lock), then faults while the child runs.
Its own C encoder objects are shared with the children the tests fork: segmentation faults on the fork children.
Net::SSLeay SSL contexts are shared with the TLS test servers it forks; SSL_new runs on a context another process freed: segmentation faults on the fork children.
The DBI/DBD::SQLite handle is shared with the child the test forks: segmentation fault on the fork child.

Its own C channel objects are shared with the publishers the tests fork: heap corruption detected on a fork child (t/03), and a segmentation fault in the parent while its children exit, before its first test (t/05).
DBD::SQLite handles are shared with the broker processes it forks: segmentation fault and invalid frees on the fork children.
DBI/DBD::SQLite handles are shared with the children the test forks (DBI reports negative active kids): segmentation fault on a fork child.

The profiler's C globals are shared with the child: the child's disable_profile clears the parent's state (wrong fork-depth counts), and segmentation faults on the fork children. t/60-forkdepth.t skips itself under perl's own fork emulation on Windows for the same reason.
Its C client and the libev loop are shared with the child the test forks: segmentation fault on the fork child.
Its C client and the libev loop are shared with the fake memcached server the tests fork: double frees on the fork children and in the parent after the children ended.

The SSL context of t/05-tls.t's server, and in t/28-fork.t Fetch's C client and loop, are shared with the children the tests fork: a segmentation fault in the parent at exit, after the server child ended (t/05-tls.t); an XS trap, then an invalid free or segmentation fault in the parent (t/28-fork.t).

Its own C container object is shared with the child: once the child closes its copy, the parent reads a closed container (wrong answer, t/07-lifetime.t), and a segmentation fault on the fork child (t/10-fork-sharing.t).
The DBD::SQLite handle is shared with the job processes Minion forks: invalid free and segmentation fault in the parent after the children ended.
The libev loop (Mojo::Reactor::EV) is shared with the socket server the tests fork: segmentation faults on the fork children.
The libev loop (AnyEvent on EV) is shared with the server the test forks: segmentation fault on the fork child.
DBD::SQLite handles are shared with the workers it forks: segmentation faults on the fork children.

Its own C arena state is shared with the children the tests fork: in t/06-fork.t a child reads the parent's cached pid and cursor (wrong answers); segmentation faults and double frees on the fork children in the others.
Net::SSLeay SSL contexts are shared by the server processes it forks: segmentation faults on the fork children.
Net::SSLeay SSL contexts are shared by the server processes it forks; SSL_new runs on a context another process freed: segmentation faults on the fork children.

The DBD::SQLite handles of its schema are shared with the test-run children it forks: segmentation fault on a fork child, and segmentation fault and double free in the parent after the children ended.
The DBD::SQLite handles of its schema are shared with the API server the test forks: segmentation fault on the fork child.
The DBD::SQLite handles of its schema are shared with the receiver daemon the tests fork: segmentation fault and double free on the fork children.
The libev loop (AnyEvent on EV) is shared with the server the test forks: segmentation fault on the fork child.
Its C logger object is shared with the child: the child logs and exits, and the parent's next log call faults (segmentation fault in the parent after the child ended).
